title: Baseball Game
description:
# Baseball Game

You are keeping score for a baseball game with unusual record operations. The record starts empty.

Given a string array `operations`, apply each operation to the current valid score record:

* An integer `x`: record a new score of `x`.
* `"+"`: record a new score equal to the sum of the previous two valid scores.
* `"D"`: record a new score equal to twice the previous valid score.
* `"C"`: invalidate and remove the previous valid score.

Return the sum of all valid scores after every operation has been applied.

The input is valid: `"+"` always has at least two previous valid scores, and `"C"` and `"D"` always have at least one previous valid score. All intermediate scores and the final answer fit in a 32-bit signed integer.

## Example 1:

**Input:** ops = ["5","2","C","D","+"]
**Output:** 30
**Explanation:** The record becomes [5], then [5,2], then [5], then [5,10], then [5,10,15]. The sum is 30.

## Example 2:

**Input:** ops = ["5","-2","4","C","D","9","+","+"]
**Output:** 27

## Example 3:

**Input:** ops = ["1","C"]
**Output:** 0

## Constraints:

* `1 <= operations.length <= 1000`
* `operations[i]` is `"C"`, `"D"`, `"+"`, or a string representing an integer in the range `[-3 * 10^4, 3 * 10^4]`.
* For operation `"+"`, there will always be at least two previous valid scores on the record.
* For operations `"C"` and `"D"`, there will always be at least one previous valid score on the record.

solutions.name: Dynamic List Stack Simulation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Represent the current valid record as a list-backed stack. Numeric operations append a score, `C` removes the last score, `D` appends twice the last score, and `+` appends the sum of the last two scores. Sum the stack after all operations.

## Key Insight

Every non-numeric command refers only to the most recent one or two valid scores, and `C` removes the most recent valid score. That is exactly the access pattern of a stack.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Manual Array Stack
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use an integer array and a `top` pointer as a manual stack. Valid scores occupy `scores[0]` through `scores[top - 1]`; each operation updates only this active prefix.

## Key Insight

The maximum number of valid scores is at most `operations.length`, so a fixed array is enough. The `top` pointer makes push and pop explicit and avoids collection overhead.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Running Total Deque Stack
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep a stack of valid scores and update the running total at the same time. When a score is added, add it to `total`; when `C` removes the latest score, subtract that removed score.

## Key Insight

The final answer is an aggregate over a mutable record. Maintaining the aggregate as the record changes avoids a second pass and highlights how undo-style updates affect totals.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Linked Node Stack with Aggregate
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build the score record as a linked stack. The top node stores the latest score and a link to the previous valid score. Maintain the total beside the linked stack.

## Key Insight

The `+` operation only needs `top.score` and `top.previous.score`, while `C` moves the top pointer back one node. This is the pointer-based version of the stack invariant and is useful for understanding linked stacks.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Recursive Operation Processor
solutions.description:
## Approach

Process operations recursively. At each index, mutate the current score stack according to the operation, then recurse to the next index. When all operations are consumed, sum the valid record.

## Key Insight

The recursion separates the idea of applying one command from the loop that advances through the command list. It is not the most practical Java style, but it is a clear way to teach the state transition for each operation.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n), for the score record and recursion stack

tests.description: The canonical sequence exercises add, cancel, double, and sum operations.
Negative scores and chained plus operations are valid.
Canceling the only score leaves an empty record.
Cancel removes the most recent doubled score before the plus operation.
Doubling and summing can produce negative record totals.
The final cancel can remove a derived score while leaving earlier derived scores.
A single numeric operation is already a complete record.
Zero can be doubled and used by plus without changing the total.
Canceling a plus-derived score exposes the previous numeric score for doubling.
Canceling a doubled negative score and deriving again keeps stack order important.
A mixed chain cancels one derived score and then derives a new one from the remaining suffix.
Consecutive cancels can empty the record before new scores are added.
